Write Chao tone numerals as IPA tone letters

Source: R/chao.R
chao_to_letters.Rd

Converts Chao tone numerals to the IPA tone letters that Chao (1930) designed them for, one letter per digit: 1 = ˩ (extra low), 2 = ˨, 3 = ˧, 4 = ˦, 5 = ˥ (extra high). For example "35" becomes ˧˥ and "214" becomes ˨˩˦.

Usage

chao_to_letters(x)

Arguments

x

A character (or integer) vector of Chao numerals, e.g. c("55", "35", "214", "51"), such as the refline or interval column of contour_to_chao().

Value

A character vector the same length as x. Elements that are NA, or that contain anything other than the digits 1 to 5, become NA (the latter with a warning).

Details

Each digit becomes one letter, so a level tone keeps both of its digits: "55" becomes ˥˥. Some descriptions write a level tone with a single letter; substr(x, 1, 1) gives that form.

Fonts with tone-letter support (Charis SIL, Doulos SIL, Gentium) join a sequence of letters into a single contour line; other fonts show the letters as separate bars. The characters are the same either way.

References

Chao, Y. R. (1930). A system of tone-letters. Le Maître Phonétique, 30, 24–27.

See also

contour_to_chao(), whose numeral columns this converts, and classify_contour() for a shape name.

Examples

chao_to_letters(c("55", "35", "214", "51"))
#> [1] "˥˥"  "˧˥"  "˨˩˦" "˥˩"
